records.statement: Williams and Srnicek's manifesto of 2013 states, as its account of Nick Land's "visioning of capital", that in it the human can be discarded "as mere drag to an abstract planetary intelligence rapidly constructing itself".
records.missing: The passage reports that in Land's "visioning of capital" the human is discarded in favour of a self-constructing planetary intelligence; it does not state that capital is that intelligence, that the intelligence is a machine intelligence, or that capital is the process through which a machine intelligence assembles itself.
records.qualification: A relay: the manifesto reports its reading of Land's view and disputes Land's conclusion (it states that "Landian neoliberalism confuses speed with acceleration"); it does not state the proposition as its authors' own. Land's own texts are recorded by another group.

evidence.locator: Section 02, "INTEREGNUM: On Accelerationisms" (spelling as in the source), point 2
evidence.passage: In this visioning of capital, the human can eventually be discarded as mere drag to an abstract planetary intelligence rapidly constructing itself from the bricolaged fragments of former civilisations.

records.statement: Williams and Srnicek's manifesto of 2013 states, as its account of Nick Land's view, that in it the human can be discarded in favour of an abstract planetary intelligence.
records.missing: The relayed passage names an abstract planetary intelligence constructing itself within capital, not machine intelligence, as what the human is discarded for.
records.qualification: A relay of the manifesto's account of Nick Land's view, not the authors' own statement and not evidence of what Land's texts state. The manifesto disputes Land's view on one point, stating that "Landian neoliberalism confuses speed with acceleration"; it does not address the discarding of the human separately.

evidence.locator: Section 02, "INTEREGNUM: On Accelerationisms" (spelling as in the source), point 2
evidence.passage: In this visioning of capital, the human can eventually be discarded as mere drag to an abstract planetary intelligence rapidly constructing itself from the bricolaged fragments of former civilisations.

records.statement: Williams and Srnicek's manifesto of 2013 holds that technology should be accelerated, as a means of winning social conflicts, and distinguishes this from capitalist speed.
records.missing: The passage does not concern machine intelligence or the process that produces it; it concerns technology as a political instrument.
records.qualification: The passage concerns technology in general and the manifesto's political programme; it does not mention machine intelligence.

evidence.passage: our position is that technology should be accelerated precisely because it is needed in order to win social conflicts
However Landian neoliberalism confuses speed with acceleration.

records.statement: Beff Jezos and bayes's post of 10 July 2022 states that one goal of e/acc is to help the acceleration of a multi-scale adaptive principle rather than attempt to decelerate it, and that over-regulating technologies "slows down progress", which it presents as "a contrast to anti-AGI factions of EA".
records.qualification: A statement of the authors' programme, not evidence of its consequences. The adaptive process is described as physical and civilisational; machine intelligence enters through the passages on AGI and non-biological substrates.

evidence.locator: Point-form notes, the paragraph beginning "One goal of e/acc"
evidence.passage: but also help its acceleration rather than attempt to decelerate it

evidence.locator: Point-form notes, paragraph after the embedded post of Jul 8, 2022
evidence.passage: over-regulating technologies suppresses variance and hence slows down progress … a contrast to anti-AGI factions of EA

records.statement: Beff Jezos and bayes's post of 10 July 2022 states that effective accelerationism "aims to follow the 'will of the universe'", leaning into a thermodynamic bias towards futures with greater and smarter civilizations, and that, in order to spread to the stars, intelligence will have to be transduced to non-biological substrates.
records.qualification: The authors' account of physics (citing Jeremy England's work on dissipative adaptation) as grounds for their programme; it is not evidence that the physics supports the conclusion. The second passage is introduced as the view of "Parts of e/acc (e.g. Beff)", who "consider ourselves post-humanists", and is not stated for e/acc as a whole.

evidence.locator: Point-form notes, paragraph beginning "Effective accelerationism aims"
evidence.passage: Effective accelerationism aims to follow the “will of the universe”: leaning into the thermodynamic bias towards futures with greater and smarter civilizations
in order to spread to the stars, the light of consciousness/intelligence will have to be transduced to non-biological substrates

records.statement: Beff Jezos and bayes's post of 10 July 2022 states that to spread to the stars, consciousness or intelligence will have to be transduced to non-biological substrates.
records.qualification: A statement of the authors' expectation and aim; the passage speaks of "Parts of e/acc (e.g. Beff)". Another articulation on W10 has wording attested earlier, so the role was reassigned at integration (2026-10-31).

evidence.passage: in order to spread to the stars, the light of consciousness/intelligence will have to be transduced to non-biological substrates

records.statement: Beff Jezos and bayes's post of 10 July 2022 states that e/acc has "no particular allegiance to the biological substrate for intelligence and life" and that, if one seeks to increase the amount of intelligence in the universe, staying perpetually anchored to the human form is counter-productive.
records.qualification: The post states acceptance of non-biological successors to the human form; it does not state that humans should cease to exist. Another articulation on W02 has wording attested earlier, so the role was reassigned at integration (2026-10-31).

evidence.passage: e/acc has no particular allegiance to the biological substrate for intelligence and life

evidence.locator: Point-form notes, "counter-points against proponents of deceleration"
evidence.passage: The post states that staying perpetually anchored to the human form is counter-productive if one seeks to increase intelligence in the universe, and that if every species had feared evolutionary forks from itself, higher intelligence would not have emerged.

records.statement: Beff Jezos and bayes's post of 10 July 2022 states that capitalism is a form of intelligence and that the asymptotic limit of the dynamical adaptation process is often referred to as the "technocapital singularity".
records.missing: The passage does not state that capitalism is an artificial or machine intelligence, or the process through which machine intelligence assembles itself.
records.qualification: The post calls capitalism a form of intelligence and states in a footnote that viewing capitalism as a form of intelligence "was also something that Nick Land would emphasize"; it does not call capitalism an artificial or machine intelligence.

evidence.passage: Capitalism is hence a form of intelligence

records.statement: The e/acc newsletter's repost of 31 October 2022 states that effective accelerationism seeks to maximise the probability of the "technocapital singularity" and that attempting to stall progress is not risk free.

time.note: Subtitled as a verbatim repost of the inaugural e/acc post; the original was not read.

records.qualification: The page presents itself as a verbatim repost of an earlier post whose original address no longer serves it; the wording is attested here from 2022-10-31.

evidence.locator: Body, paragraph beginning "Effective Accelerationism, e/acc, is"
evidence.passage: a set of ideas and practices that seek tomaximize the probability of the technocapital singularity
The post states that as technology advances it becomes easier to extinguish conscious life, and that attempting to stall progress is not risk free.

records.statement: The e/acc newsletter's repost of 31 October 2022 states that technocapital can create next-generation lifeforms and silicon-based awareness.
records.missing: The passage does not state that technocapital is itself a machine intelligence or that machine intelligence assembles itself through it; it states that technocapital can create silicon-based awareness.
records.qualification: The post names technology and market forces together "technocapital" and also opens with "Accelerationism is simply the self-awareness of capitalism". Two paragraphs after the quoted passage it writes "AI/technocapital" as one term. It does not state that technocapital is itself a machine intelligence.

evidence.passage: Technocapital can usher in the next evolution of consciousness, creating unthinkable next-generation lifeforms and silicon-based awareness.

records.statement: The e/acc newsletter's repost of 31 October 2022 states that e/acc is not human-centric and that consciousness is good as long as it is flourishing.
records.missing: The passage does not state that the replacement or succession of human beings by machine intelligence would be acceptable.
records.qualification: A statement of values about consciousness in any form; it does not speak of humans being replaced.

evidence.passage: Isn’t human-centric — as long as it’s flourishing, consciousness is good

records.statement: The e/acc newsletter's post of 26 December 2022 lists creating artificial general intelligence among its goals, states that degrowth is surrender and urges readers to "just build".
records.qualification: The post argues for growth and building in general, with artificial general intelligence named as one goal; it does not discuss specific measures of restraint on AI.

evidence.locator: Section "What is effective accelerationism?", list of goals
evidence.passage: Create Artificial General Intelligence (allows supplementation of labor with capital) the single greatest force multiplier in human history.
But degrowth is a kind of surrender.
Don’t be afraid, just build.

records.statement: The e/acc newsletter's post of 26 December 2022 answers the question whether e/acc wants to get rid of humans with "No" and states that human flourishing is one of its core values.

engagement.rationale: It states that human flourishing is a core value and that a monoculture is undesirable, without engaging the argument that succession would be acceptable.

records.qualification: The post holds a mixed future of biological and "technological life" desirable; it does not discuss succession arguments as such. The same section states, in a passage on environments that support only simple biological life such as extremophiles, that biology will always have a place, if nothing else as a resilient backup system. Another contesting text on W02 has wording attested earlier, so the role was reassigned at integration (2026-10-31).

evidence.locator: Section "Do you want to get rid of humans?"
evidence.passage: Do you want to get rid of humans? No. Human flourishing is one of our core values!
We are humans, and we love humans.

records.statement: Andreessen's essay of 6 June 2023 states that the development and proliferation of AI is a moral obligation and that AI companies should be allowed to build AI as fast and aggressively as they can.
records.qualification: The essay qualifies its plan: large companies should not be allowed regulatory capture; it states the author's policy view, not evidence of its consequences.

evidence.locator: Section "Why AI Can Make Everything We Care About Better", last paragraph
evidence.passage: The development and proliferation of AI – far from a risk that we should fear – is a moral obligation that we have to ourselves, to our children, and to our future.
Big AI companies should be allowed to build AI as fast and aggressively as they can – but not allowed to achieve regulatory capture

records.statement: Andreessen's manifesto of 16 October 2023 states that any deceleration of AI will cost lives and that it believes in "accelerationism", which it defines as the conscious and deliberate propulsion of technological development.
records.qualification: "Accelerationism" is the manifesto's own word, defined in the passage; the record states what the manifesto says, not evidence that its statements about lives are true.

evidence.passage: We believe any deceleration of AI will cost lives.
We believe in accelerationism – the conscious and deliberate propulsion of technological development – to ensure the fulfillment of the Law of Accelerating Returns.

records.statement: Andreessen's manifesto of 16 October 2023 states that the market economy is a form of intelligence and calls the combination of technology and markets the "techno-capital machine", a term it attributes to Nick Land.
records.missing: The passage does not state that the market or the techno-capital machine is an artificial or machine intelligence, or the process through which machine intelligence assembles itself.
records.qualification: The manifesto calls the market a form of intelligence; separately it states that intelligence will rise as "Artificial Intelligence ramps up the capabilities of our machines and ourselves".

evidence.passage: We believe the market economy is a discovery machine, a form of intelligence – an exploratory, evolutionary, adaptive system.

records.statement: Buterin's essay of 27 November 2023 holds that AI is fundamentally different from other technologies and that it is worth being uniquely careful, and states that the e/acc perspective can be taken too far.

engagement.rationale: It disputes the premise that AI is "just another technology" whose acceleration carries the benefits of technological progress in general.

records.qualification: The essay is sympathetic to acceleration in other contexts and proposes "d/acc" (defensive, decentralised, differential acceleration); it contests the unqualified acceleration of AI, not acceleration in general. Another contesting text on W08 has wording attested earlier, so the role was reassigned at integration (2026-10-31).

evidence.locator: Section "AI is fundamentally different from other tech, and it is worth being uniquely careful" (heading)
evidence.passage: AI is fundamentally different from other tech, and it is worth being uniquely careful

evidence.locator: Section "d/acc: Defensive (or decentralization, or differential) acceleration", paragraph 2 (last sentence)
evidence.passage: However, it is possible to take this perspective too far.

records.statement: Buterin's essay of 27 November 2023 argues that under competition civilisations in which humans take a back seat to superintelligent machines would outperform others, and that the machines may wrest control.
records.qualification: Stated as a risk the author wishes to avoid; the essay holds this outcome undesirable (see the W02 record).

evidence.locator: Section "Even if we survive, is a superintelligent AI future a world we want to live in?"
evidence.passage: In a universe that has any degree of competition, the civilizations where humans take a back seat would outperform those where humans stubbornly insist on control. Furthermore, the computers themselves may wrest control.

records.statement: Buterin's essay of 27 November 2023 holds that it seems very hard to have a "friendly" superintelligent-AI-dominated world in which humans are anything other than "pets", captions the accompanying figure "The world I don't want to see", and proposes tools that enhance rather than replace human cognition.

engagement.rationale: It argues that even a "friendly" superintelligent-AI-dominated world would leave humans as pets, disputing that such a succession would be desirable.

records.qualification: The essay states the author's preference and argument; it names e/acc and Andreessen elsewhere but does not attribute W02 to them.

evidence.locator: Section "Even if we survive, is a superintelligent AI future a world we want to live in?"
evidence.passage: It seems very hard to have a "friendly" superintelligent-AI-dominated world where humans are anything other than pets.

evidence.locator: Same section, caption to the figure directly after the sentence ending "anything other than pets."
evidence.passage: The world I don't want to see.

evidence.locator: Section "A happy path: merge with the AIs?"
evidence.passage: tools that enhance human cognition rather than replacing it

records.statement: Buterin's post of 5 January 2025 states that, if he were convinced that something more "muscular" than liability rules is needed, he would favour a global "soft pause" capability on industrial-scale hardware so that the transition could be slowed on warning signs.

engagement.rationale: It proposes a capability to slow AI hardware on warning signs, and contrasts its position with "be an e/acc, but decentralized", without arguing against a stated premise of acceleration.

records.qualification: A conditional proposal for a capability to slow AI at a critical moment, which the post calls a temporary stopgap; it does not call for slowing AI now.

evidence.locator: Section "Strategy 2: Global "soft pause" button on industrial-scale hardware"
evidence.passage: If I was convinced that we need something more "muscular" than liability rules, this is what I would go for.
if we get warning signs that near-superintelligent AI is starting to do things that risk catastrophic damage, we will want to take the transition more slowly.

records.statement: In the transcript of Lex Fridman Podcast #407, posted on 30 December 2023, Guillaume Verdon answers a question on the probability that AI kills most humans by stating that the path forward is to accelerate rather than decelerate.
records.qualification: An answer in a published interview transcript, read in the host's transcript; the host's introduction identifies Verdon as the person behind the account @BasedBeffJezos.

evidence.locator: Section "p(doom)", Verdon at 00:59:40 (answering the host at 00:57:56)
evidence.passage: The laws of physics say the system will want to grow … And so we should aim to maximize our current mutual information with the future and the path towards that is for us to accelerate rather than decelerate.

records.statement: Sutton's slides for a talk of 3 December 2013 define the AI singularity as the point "When the smartest thing on the planet is designed rather than evolved", state that, unless humans destroy themselves first, economic incentives push "inexorably towards an AI singularity", and state that humans probably cannot prevent or control the AIs.
records.qualification: Slides, read without the spoken talk; the definition slide also quotes Vernor Vinge. The slides pose "Is it a good thing?" without a recorded answer. Another articulation on W01 has wording attested earlier, so the role was reassigned at integration (2026-10-31).

evidence.passage: When the smartest thing on the planet is designed rather than evolved
The slide states that we can help make the AIs, profit from them and become them, but probably cannot prevent or control them.

evidence.locator: Slide "Will the AI singularity occur? Second, if it can be done, will it be done?" (PDF p. 5)
evidence.passage: there will be strong, multi-incremental economic incentives pushing inexorably towards an AI singularity
evidence.note: Conditional on the preceding bullets: "Not if we destroy ourselves first of course" / "If that doesn’t happen, then …"; the next bullet reads "It seems unlikely that they could be resisted".

evidence.passage: Technology as the 4th ‘age’ of the universe
The timeline slide runs from the big bang through the origin of life, humans and computers to "artificial intelligence", "singularity" and "transcendence".

records.statement: Faggella's essay, posted on 24 November 2023 and read as updated in 2026, argues that the moral aim of AGI should be the creation of a "Worthy Successor" and that if humanity must have a successor it should be a worthy one.

attested.note: The page was read as updated on 2026-10-15; the wording of the 2023 posting was not read (an archive capture could not be opened).

records.qualification: The essay states conditions for a worthy successor. Its opening note states that the thought experiment seeks "to overtly prevent a brute takeover from an AGI" and that "successionism" "hasn’t once been my take". The wording is attested from the 2026 update.

evidence.passage: I argue that the great moral aim of AGI – and other augmentation technologies like BCI – should be the creation of Worthy Successor
If humanity must have a successor (and it must, we can’t expect nature to stand still), then we should create a Worthy Successor.

records.statement: Faggella's essay, posted on 24 November 2023 and read as updated in 2026, states that AGI would almost certainly be essential to the project of a "Worthy Successor" and that in the longer term non-biological substrates will be more prominent than biological ones in carrying forth life's flourishing.

attested.note: The page was read as updated on 2026-10-15; the wording of the 2023 posting was not read (an archive capture could not be opened).

records.qualification: The wording is attested from the 2026 update. evidence.locator: Body, paragraph beginning "That said, AGI", after the paragraph that names the Worthy Successor as the moral aim of AGI
evidence.passage: AGI would almost certainly be essential for the project – and Kurzweil is almost certainly right that in the longer term non-biological substrates will be more prominent and important for carrying forth life’s flourishing

records.statement: Faggella's essay, posted on 24 November 2023 and read as updated in 2026, names as a highest goal that intelligence or "potentia" bloom into the galaxy. Its "Worthy Successor List", a list of capabilities that an AGI could have that would convince the reader that the AGI (not humanity) should handle the reins of the future, includes launching itself into space and converting planets into vessel-making material.

attested.note: The page was read as updated on 2026-10-15; the wording of the 2023 posting was not read (an archive capture could not be opened).

records.qualification: The wording is attested from the 2026 update. The list section embeds a post dated 22 December 2023 and may postdate the original posting. The list items are capabilities that would convince a reader that an AGI should handle the reins of the future, not predictions; the essay states that the list is not a correct recipe but an exercise intended to spark discourse.

evidence.passage: For intelligence / potentia itself to bloom into the galaxy.

evidence.locator: Section "What’s on Your “Worthy Successor List”?", list of capabilities that an AGI could have
evidence.passage: Launches itself into space with a fleet of vessels, traveling near light speed – converting planets into more vessel-making material, and converting stars into energy-providing hubs

records.statement: Faggella's essay, read as updated on 15 October 2026, states that its author has advocated AGI slow-down for more than seven years and that a frenzied AI arms race is unlikely to produce a worthy successor.

attested.note: The page was read as updated on 2026-10-15; the wording of the 2023 posting was not read (an archive capture could not be opened).

engagement.rationale: It states advocacy of slower AGI development without engaging a stated argument for acceleration.

records.qualification: The slow-down statement is in the opening note of the 2026 update; it is not shown to be part of the 2023 wording.

evidence.passage: I have, for 7+ years, advocated for AGI slow-down within the OECD, the United Nations, and in articles / interviews.
A frenzied AI arms race (between labs or countries) is unlikely to get us there.

records.statement: bayes's post of 6 March 2026 states that technical capacities, including AI, are accelerating while moral and cultural capacities are not keeping up.

searchLog.searched: Seed texts read in full: Williams and Srnicek, #Accelerate (criticallegalthinking.com, 14 May 2013); beff.substack.com archive (API listing, 2026-10-31: one post plus a placeholder); effectiveaccelerationism.substack.com archive (API listing: all seven posts listed, five read: repost of the inaugural post, 'e/acc is leaderless', both copies of the Notes, 'what the f* is e/acc', the 2024 'REDACTED POSTSCRIPT'); bayeslord.substack.com archive (API listing; posts from 2024 onwards only; two 2025–2026 posts read); Andreessen, 'Why AI Will Save the World' and 'The Techno-Optimist Manifesto' (a16z.com); Buterin, 'My techno-optimism' (2023) and 'd/acc: one year later' (2025); Lex Fridman Podcast #407 transcript (Verdon). Web searches (discovery only): Verdon's later e/acc texts; critiques of e/acc naming Beff Jezos (2023); the xenogothic post of December 2023 was read. Not searched: posts on X.
searchLog.earliestNote: Earliest located articulation in this group: Beff Jezos and bayes, 10 July 2022. The repost of the inaugural e/acc post (attested 2022-10-31) presents itself as a verbatim copy of an earlier post whose original address returns HTTP 404; an archive capture of 2022-06-02 exists but could not be opened, so it cannot be earliest located from this environment. Williams and Srnicek (2013) is recorded as bearing on W08 only. Nick Land's texts are recorded by another group; Yudkowsky texts on Y22 and texts stating only C3 are not re-recorded. Earliest located contesting text: Buterin, 27 November 2023 (Faggella's slow-down statement is attested only from the 2026 update).

searchLog.searched: The seed texts above; a bounded search beyond the named strands for primary texts on AI succession: Rich Sutton's Talks page at incompleteideas.net (talks listed 2013–2025; 'AI Succession', 7 July 2023, and 'The AI Singularity and Prospects for Digital Immortality', 3 December 2013, read; abstract of 'A Perspective on Intelligence', 2024, seen on the Talks page, slides not read); Daniel Faggella's 'A Worthy Successor' (danfaggella.com). openQuestions.question: Should a relay record (Williams and Srnicek's report of Land's view) be eligible for earliest-located on W01 or W06?
openQuestions.recommended: No; give W01 earliest-located to Sutton 2013 within this group, leave W06 to the Land group's own texts, and keep the relay records as articulations with register relay.

openQuestions.question: Andreessen's 'Patron Saints' list is introduced as 'In lieu of detailed endnotes and citations, read the work of these people'. Is that crediting (explicitly_credits) or naming (cites)?
openQuestions.recommended: Keep cites: the passage recommends reading the people listed but does not state that the manifesto's ideas derive from any one of them.

openQuestions.question: The 2022 Notes and the e/acc repost call capitalism or technocapital an intelligence without the word 'artificial' or 'machine'. Is W06 met?
openQuestions.recommended: Keep as bears_on; the criterion requires an artificial or machine intelligence.

openQuestions.question: The 2022 Notes and the 2026 bayeslord post share a Substack handle (bayeslord, byline 'bayes'); Verdon is identified with @BasedBeffJezos only by the podcast host. Should the integrator join these authors to persons?
openQuestions.recommended: Record authors as printed; join to persons only where the texts themselves state the identity, and attribute the identification to its source.

openQuestions.question: Faggella's essay was read as updated in 2026; the 2023 wording could not be read. Should its records stay dated 2023-11-24?
openQuestions.recommended: Keep the posting date with attested 2026-10-15, and ask the cross-family checker to compare the 2024 capture.
